name: Oats (rolled or steel-cut)
notes: Beta-glucan soluble fiber helps lower LDL cholesterol and slows glucose absorption.

name: Fatty fish (salmon, sardines, mackerel)
notes: Two servings/week is the widely cited target for omega-3 intake (WHO/FAO guidance).

name: Extra virgin olive oil
notes: Cornerstone of the Mediterranean diet, associated with cardiovascular risk reduction.

name: Berries (blueberries, strawberries, blackberries)
notes: Anthocyanins are antioxidants studied for vascular and cognitive health.

name: Leafy greens (spinach, kale, broccoli)
notes: Dietary nitrates support healthy blood pressure; vitamin K supports bone.

name: Garlic
notes: Allicin is studied for modest blood-pressure and lipid effects.

name: Nuts (almonds, walnuts mix)
notes: A small daily handful is associated with reduced cardiovascular risk.

name: Walnuts
notes: Richest nut source of plant omega-3 (ALA); studied for cognitive support.

name: Turmeric
notes: Curcumin is anti-inflammatory; better absorbed with black pepper (piperine).

name: Eggs
notes: Choline supports brain cell membranes; yolks carry lutein for eye health.

name: Dark chocolate (70%+ cocoa)
notes: Cocoa flavanols are studied for blood flow and cognition; keep portions small.

name: Green tea
notes: EGCG is an antioxidant studied for metabolic and liver support.

name: Coffee (filtered)
notes: Regular moderate coffee intake is associated with lower liver scarring risk.

name: Beetroot
notes: Nitrates convert to nitric oxide, supporting vessel flexibility.

name: Water
notes: Adequate hydration is the single most important habit for kidney health.

name: Cabbage & cruciferous vegetables
notes: Low-potassium cruciferous option studied for kidney-friendly diets.

name: Ginger
notes: Gingerols are studied for nausea relief and airway relaxation.

name: Citrus fruits (orange, grapefruit, lemon)
notes: Vitamin C supports immune cell function and collagen synthesis.

name: Tomatoes (raw or cooked)
notes: Cooking increases lycopene availability — a rare case where processed is better.

name: Yogurt with live cultures
notes: Live-culture fermented foods replenish beneficial gut microbes.

name: High-fiber foods (beans, lentils, whole grains)
notes: Fiber feeds gut bacteria and feeds almost every organ downstream.

name: Cinnamon (Ceylon)
notes: Ceylon cinnamon is preferred long-term (lower coumarin than cassia).

name: Fenugreek seeds
notes: Studied for improving post-meal glucose response.

name: Beans & lentils
notes: Low glycemic index staple associated with better sugar control.

name: Bitter melon
notes: Traditional remedy studied for glucose-lowering effects.

name: Dairy (milk, yogurt, kefir, cheese)
notes: Primary dietary iodine source in many countries.

name: Avocado
notes: Supports skin barrier and lipid profiles.

name: Sweet potato
notes: Beta-carotene converts to vitamin A, central to skin renewal and vision.

name: Carrots
notes: Classic source of vitamin A precursors for retinal health.

name: Mushrooms (shiitake, maitake)
notes: Beta-glucans are studied immunomodulators.

name: Seaweed (nori, kelp)
notes: Iodine-dense; small amounts suffice — excess can harm the thyroid.

name: Brazil nuts
notes: 1-2 nuts/day covers selenium needs for thyroid hormone conversion.

name: Fish oil / omega-3 (EPA+DHA) supplement
notes: Studied for triglyceride reduction; choose third-party-tested brands.

name: Vitamin D3 supplement
notes: Most adults in northern latitudes have low winter levels; test before high doses.

name: Magnesium supplement (glycinate/citrate)
notes: Involved in 300+ enzyme reactions; studied for blood pressure and sleep.

name: Probiotic supplement (multi-strain)
notes: Strain-specific effects matter; food sources are first-line.

name: Curcumin supplement (with piperine)
notes: Concentrated anti-inflammatory; can interact with blood thinners.

name: Psyllium husk
notes: Evidence-backed for constipation and LDL cholesterol reduction.

name: Collagen peptides
notes: Small trials support skin elasticity and joint comfort.

name: Lutein & zeaxanthin supplement
notes: AREDS2 trial nutrients for macular health.
